---
title: "Figure 12.1: Response to Terms-of-Trade Shock by Anchoring Level"
---

![Python: `python/fig-12-1.py`](../images/python/fig-12-1.png)

The response of inflation and consumption to a terms-of-trade shock, after 6
and 12 months, in countries with strongly and weakly anchored inflation
expectations.

**New in this chart:**

- a three-row table of labels below the bars;
- colours set per bar.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Error bars missing

The published chart has error bars (90 percent confidence intervals). Those
values are not part of the data extracted from the Excel chart, so the
Python version cannot draw them.
:::

## The data

Sheet `data`, 8 rows, a single unnamed series:

| series_0 |
|---|
| 0.0026 |
| ... |

Excel's chart had no series name and no category labels that the extraction
could read. The column is therefore called `series_0`, and all labels are
typed into the script from the published chart.

## The script

### Labels and colours

```python
horizons = ["6m", "12m"] * 4
anchoring = ["Strongly\nanchored", "Weakly\nanchored"] * 2
outcomes = ["Inflation", "Consumption"]
bar_colours = ["#A6A6A6", "#A6A6A6", "#A678B5", "#A678B5"] * 2
```

Multiplying a list repeats it, so `["6m", "12m"] * 4` gives eight labels, one
per bar. The bars come in this order:

1. inflation, strongly anchored, 6m and 12m;
2. inflation, weakly anchored, 6m and 12m;
3. the same four for consumption.

The colour list follows the same pattern: grey for strongly anchored and
purple for weakly anchored.

```python
x = np.arange(1, len(data) + 1)
ax.bar(x, data["series_0"], width=0.55, color=bar_colours)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
```

### The table below the plot

```python
trans = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
rows = {"horizon": -0.05, "anchoring": -0.15, "outcome": -0.29}
for xi in np.arange(0.5, 9, 1):
    if xi in (0.5, 4.5, 8.5):
        depth = -0.33
    elif xi in (2.5, 6.5):
        depth = -0.22
    else:
        depth = -0.09
    ax.plot([xi, xi], [0, depth], color="black", linewidth=0.6,
            transform=trans, clip_on=False)
```

The table has three rows: horizon, anchoring level and outcome. The vertical
separators come in three lengths:

- **Between the two horizons** of a pair: short (9 percent of the plot
  height), through the first row only.
- **Between anchoring levels**: medium (22 percent), through two rows.
- **Between inflation and consumption**, and at both ends: long (33
  percent), through all three rows.

`if ... elif ... else` picks the length for each position. The `rows`
dictionary holds the height of each row's text below the axis.

```python
for xi, label in zip(x, horizons):
    ax.text(xi, rows["horizon"], label, ha="center", va="center", transform=trans)
for centre, label in zip((1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5), anchoring):
    ax.text(centre, rows["anchoring"], label, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=trans, linespacing=1.0)
for centre, label in zip((2.5, 6.5), outcomes):
    ax.text(centre, rows["outcome"], label, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=trans)
```

Each label is centred under the bars it describes:

- **Horizons**: under each bar.
- **Anchoring levels**: under each pair of bars (1.5, 3.5, ...).
- **Outcomes**: under each group of four bars (2.5 and 6.5).

All the text uses `transform=trans`, so x is in data units and y in fractions
of the plot height. See [Tables of labels below the
plot](../techniques.qmd#sec-label-tables).

```python
ax.set_xlim(0.5, 8.5)
ax.set_xticks([])

set_y_scale(ax, -1.2, 1.2, 0.4)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter("{x:.1f}")
```

The normal tick labels are switched off, because the table replaces them.
`new_chart()` was called with `bottom_gap=0.95`, enough room for three rows.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-12-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-12-1.py"}
"""
Figure 12.1: Response to Terms-of-Trade Shock by Anchoring Level.

The published chart also shows error bars (90 percent confidence intervals).
Those values are not part of the data extracted from the Excel chart, so
they are not drawn here.
"""
import numpy as np

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart, set_y_scale

STEM = "fig-12-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

# The labels are not part of the extracted data; they are taken from the
# published chart. Bars come in pairs (6 and 12 months) for each anchoring
# level, first for inflation, then for consumption.
horizons = ["6m", "12m"] * 4
anchoring = ["Strongly\nanchored", "Weakly\nanchored"] * 2
outcomes = ["Inflation", "Consumption"]
bar_colours = ["#A6A6A6", "#A6A6A6", "#A678B5", "#A678B5"] * 2

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Response to Terms-of-Trade Shock\nby Anchoring Level",
    subtitle="(Percentage points)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Barrett and others (forthcoming); Bems and others (2021); and\n"
        "IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: Cumulative response to month-on-month percentage change in the\n"
        "commodity terms-of-trade index (Gruss and Kebhaj 2019). Each country-\n"
        "year is classified as strongly (weakly) anchored when it is in the top\n"
        "(bottom) 25 percent of the observations of the anchoring index. Error bars\n"
        "denote 90 percent confidence intervals."
    ),
    left=0.45,
    right=0.15,
    bottom_gap=0.95,
)

x = np.arange(1, len(data) + 1)
ax.bar(x, data["series_0"], width=0.55, color=bar_colours)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)

# A three-row table of labels below the plot: horizon, anchoring level and
# outcome, with separators of increasing length.
trans = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
rows = {"horizon": -0.05, "anchoring": -0.15, "outcome": -0.29}
for xi in np.arange(0.5, 9, 1):
    if xi in (0.5, 4.5, 8.5):
        depth = -0.33
    elif xi in (2.5, 6.5):
        depth = -0.22
    else:
        depth = -0.09
    ax.plot([xi, xi], [0, depth], color="black", linewidth=0.6,
            transform=trans, clip_on=False)
for xi, label in zip(x, horizons):
    ax.text(xi, rows["horizon"], label, ha="center", va="center", transform=trans)
for centre, label in zip((1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5), anchoring):
    ax.text(centre, rows["anchoring"], label, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=trans, linespacing=1.0)
for centre, label in zip((2.5, 6.5), outcomes):
    ax.text(centre, rows["outcome"], label, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=trans)

ax.set_xlim(0.5, 8.5)
ax.set_xticks([])

set_y_scale(ax, -1.2, 1.2, 0.4)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter("{x:.1f}")
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
